clue.text: Quiet before walk because of unsteady gait

parts.note: SH is the call for quiet
to amble is to walk at a leisurely pace

explanation.surface: Someone tiptoes quietly before setting off on a stroll, and that explains their wobbly way of walking.
explanation.definitionFit: A shamble is an awkward, shuffling way of moving, which is an unsteady walk.

clue.text: This model is about the right size

indicators.note: about shows the model goes round the other letter

parts.note: a statue is a sculpted model of a figure

explanation.surface: A fashion model claims to be just the correct dimensions.
explanation.definitionFit: Stature is a person's height, their physical scale.

clue.text: Lady in an awful pale colour

indicators.note: in shows one word is put inside the other

explanation.surface: A woman wearing a dreadfully washed-out shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen describes a deathly grey pallor, the shade of wood ash.

clue.text: Red colours of sort of tree found in footwear

indicators.note: found in shows the jumbled letters sit inside the footwear
sort of suggests the word tree is rearranged into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: The crimson shades of some kind of tree turn up inside shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' makes EETR from TREE; 'found in' places it inside BOOTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Beetroot is a deep purplish-red, so beetroots are colours of that shade.

clue.text: Turn out to be some sort of third rate vice

indicators.note: some sort of suggests the word vice is reworked into another arrangement
third asks for the third letter of the word rate

explanation.surface: A third-rate vice proves to be a mild sort of wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some sort of' makes EVIC from VICE; 'third' takes T, the third letter of 'rate'.
explanation.definitionFit: To evict is to expel a tenant, throwing them out of their home.

clue.text: Inclined towards a career as a cobbler

explanation.surface: Someone leaning towards a life of mending shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: A ship heeling leans over to one side; a cobbler spends their working life heeling, putting new heels on shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel heeling tilts over in the wind, and a shoe repairer's trade includes fitting new heels to footwear.

clue.text: Spot drunk isn't heavy

explanation.surface: A stain left by a drinker who is not weighty.
explanation.definitionFit: A highlight is a bright spot, the part of a picture that catches the light.

clue.text: Soldier held up by the returning crew

indicators.note: held shows the soldier is contained within the other letters
returning means the word the is read backwards
up turns the soldier upside down, as fits a down clue

explanation.surface: A soldier delayed by the oarsmen coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns GI into IG; 'returning' turns THE into EHT; 'held' puts IG inside EHT.
explanation.definitionFit: An eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen.

clue.text: Provides protection from snail with suet!

indicators.note: from suggests the answer is made out of the letters of the following words, rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener's trick: a snail mixed with suet keeps plants safe.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulates means shields or covers to prevent heat, sound or electricity passing through.

clue.text: Varnishes over government leader's defeats

indicators.note: leader's asks for the first letter of the word government

explanation.surface: A head of state glosses over the electoral setbacks of the ruling party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is a link; the surface leans on the phrase 'glosses over'.
explanation.definitionFit: Glosses are shiny coatings, so as a verb it means puts a sheen on, as varnish does.

clue.text: Hurting the final half dozen in reaching goal

indicators.note: in tells us these pieces go inside the other word
final asks for the closing letter of the word the

parts.note: six is VI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An athlete in pain over the last six steps still manages to get to the finishing line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts E (the final letter of 'the') plus VI inside ACHING, after ACHI.
explanation.definitionFit: Achieving something is arriving at what you set out to do, a target attained.

clue.text: Force us to give energy

parts.note: G is the symbol for gravitational force, as in pulling 5g

explanation.surface: A demand that we be compelled to hand over our vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto is hearty enjoyment and vigour, a lively drive in doing something.

clue.text: Useful narrow part of a bone

indicators.note: part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that come before it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A handy slender piece of a skeleton.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'bone' as the definition, but ULNAR is an adjective, so the definition is 'of a bone' and 'part' alone signals the hidden word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulnar describes things relating to the ulna, the long forearm bone on the little-finger side.

clue.text: All settle somehow, but give false accounts

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters of all settle are put together in some other way

explanation.surface: Everyone reaches an agreement, yet lies about what happened.
explanation.definitionFit: To tell tales is to spread untrue or malicious stories about others.

clue.text: Using a measure of excuse in middle age

parts.note: an em is a printer's measure of width
a ploy is a ruse or pretext

indicators.note: middle asks for the central letter of the word age

explanation.surface: Someone resorting to a dodge as a way of explaining away their midlife crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: The em is a typesetting unit; the middle letter of 'age' is G.
explanation.definitionFit: Employing a tool is putting it to work, making use of it.

clue.text: He claims to be academic

explanation.surface: A man insists that he is a scholar.
explanation.walkthrough: One who professes is one who claims; it is also a senior university teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A professor is one who professes, declaring a belief openly, and also a university's senior teacher.

clue.text: Price increases in the apartment which no one backed

indicators.note: backed means the letters of no one are read backwards

parts.note: NO plus I, the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Rents go up in a flat nobody supported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns NOI (NO plus I for one) into ION.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflation is the general rise in prices over time.

clue.text: Puts it on one end in the ship

indicators.note: in shows these letters are placed within the ship

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, a ship's name prefix

indicators.note: end asks for the last letter of the word one

explanation.surface: Someone stands a thing upright on its end aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places IT plus E (the end of 'one') inside SS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sites as a verb means places or positions, as in siting a building.

clue.text: Feeling suffocated, he stormed out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of he stormed are put out of their order

explanation.surface: A man feeling stifled leaves the room in a rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like part of 'stormed out'; it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Smothered means stifled or unable to breathe, as under a heavy blanket.

clue.text: Posts letters when rash

indicators.note: the letters of posts are treated as loose letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sends mail in a hasty, reckless moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rash' looks like an adjective about the poster; it is the noun, a skin eruption.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash is an outbreak of red blotches on the skin.

clue.text: Eclipse is almost certain to disappear

indicators.note: almost says the last letter of the word for certain is dropped

parts.note: to pass away is to disappear

explanation.surface: A solar eclipse is very likely to vanish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims SURE to SUR.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse someone is to outshine or exceed them.

clue.text: Stupidly plump and shifty including beginnings of ugly old Una

indicators.note: including shows the first pair of words surrounds the other letters
beginnings of asks for the first letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: A tubby, untrustworthy character foolishly takes in an unattractive elderly woman named Una.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' puts UOU (first letters of 'ugly old Una') between FAT and SLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatuously means in a silly, foolishly complacent manner, which is acting without sense.

clue.text: Fluttered eyelid at Des first then gave up

indicators.note: fluttered suggests the letters of eyelid flit into a new order
first asks for the first letter of the name Des

explanation.surface: Someone batted an eyelash at a man called Des, then surrendered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fluttered' makes YIELDE from EYELID; 'first' adds D from Des.
explanation.definitionFit: Yielded means surrendered or conceded.

clue.text: These help us to cook the roasts

definitions.text: These help us to cook the roasts

indicators.note: to cook is to fiddle or tamper with, so the letters of the roasts are jumbled

explanation.surface: A description of kitchen controls that let us roast meat.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes the devices; 'cook' also signals an anagram of THE ROASTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheostats are variable resistors, used to regulate the heat of electric ovens and hobs.

clue.text: The view was observed by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word is to be heard, not spelt

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that the vista was spotted, judging by what they heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A scene is a landscape or vista spread before the eyes.

clue.text: Discerning first secretary acted piously in the ad

annotationWithheld.why: Discerning first secretary acted piously in the ad (5): S + A(PI)D reads only if 'acted' gives nothing, and 'Discerning' does not define SAPID (tasty); the clue as held looks garbled and no source gives the printed text.
annotationWithheld.clue: Discerning first secretary acted piously in the ad

clue.text: Possess about a pound, then reduce it by 50p

indicators.note: about shows the first word goes round the other letter

parts.note: L stands for a pound, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: Own a pound coin, then knock fifty pence off it.
explanation.walkthrough: Halving a pound takes 50p off it, so the definition is witty and exact.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting a pound into two equal parts leaves fifty pence, a reduction by a half.

clue.text: Ring up about one shrub for the garden

indicators.note: about shows the ring word goes round the other letter
up in a down clue means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Phone round about a single bush to plant outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts I inside CALL to give CALIL; 'up' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilac is a flowering bush with fragrant purple or white blooms.

clue.text: Goes from the dais leading towards the door

definitions.text: Goes from the dais leading towards the door

indicators.note: from the says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A bride walks away from the platform down to the exit.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'dais leading'; read whole, the clue describes the walkway from the front to the door.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is the passage between pews, running from the front of a church to its entrance.

clue.text: Little devil Eric nearly led towards destruction

definitions.text: Little devil Eric nearly led towards destruction

parts.note: an imp is a little devil

indicators.note: nearly says the last letter of the name Eric is dropped

explanation.surface: A mischievous child named Eric almost leads someone to ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: The American spelling has one L. Read whole, the clue describes being put in danger.
explanation.definitionFit: Imperiled means put in jeopardy, exposed to harm or ruin.

clue.text: Boy took in press operator

indicators.note: took in shows one word holds the other inside it

explanation.surface: A lad welcomed a journalist who was a factory worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'operator' suggests a machine worker; a surgeon operates on patients.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon performs operations, so is one who operates.

clue.text: Inferred foreign nobleman got in the act

indicators.note: got in shows the nobleman goes inside the act

explanation.surface: A deduction made because an overseas aristocrat joined the play.
explanation.definitionFit: Deduced means worked out by reasoning, concluded from evidence.
